1.

In a complaint submitted by the respondent/complainant, hereinafter being referred as respondent only, for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420, 467, 468,
471 of Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has been summoned as an accused.

2. Aggrieved of the abovementioned order, the present petition under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, has been filed with a prayer for quashing of summoning order dated 20.12.2025, hereinafter being referred to as 'impugned order', passed by the Court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate Balachaur, District SBS Nagar, hereinafter being referred to as 'trial Court'.

entities.text: Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate Balachaur, District SBS Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The complaint, too, has been sought to be quashed.

3. In nut-shell, the facts emerging from record are that a complaint was filed by the respondent alleging therein that the petitioner was elected as CRM-M-6117-2026 (O&M) a Sarpanch of Village Natha Nangal, and that while misusing his abovementioned position, he had misappropriated Government fund.

It was alleged by the respondent that the petitioner by tampering the Panchayat record fraudulently disbursed the fund pertaining to Shagun Scheme, Bhudhapa Pension, Widow Pension, MNREGA Scheme and funds under other heads.
The specific instances of mis-appropriation were given by the respondent in detail.
Once the abovementioned complaint was filed, the learned trial Court asked the respondent to lead preliminary evidence and the abovesaid preliminary evidence was duly adduced by the respondent.

In the preliminary evidence, the respondent examined the following witnesses:-

sentences.text: On appreciation of abovementioned documentary as well as oral evidence, the learned trial Court while discussing the abovementioned documentary as well as oral evidence, observed that the allegations with regard to disbursement of funds to Pyara Singh under MNREGA Scheme and Panchayat Government Scheme were prima facie true and that the same amounted to an act of fraud.

With regard to abovementioned act, it has been observed by the learned trial Court that the presence of abovementioned person had been marked and wages disbursed to him by showing him a worker at two different places on one day.

While observing that it is not possible that a person would work at two places on the same day, and draw double wages, the learned trial Court summoned the petitioner to face trial for the commission of offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
6. Aggrieved of the abovementioned order, the present petition has been filed.

7. Heard.
8.

It has been contended on behalf of petitioner that instant case is a case, wherein the complaint has been filed on the basis of false allegations and that the only motive of the respondent behind the filing of complaint is the political rivalry.

According to learned counsel for the petitioner, the respondent is an arch rival of the petitioner and he had been unsuccessfully contesting the election against the petitioner, and when he could not succeed in the election, the respondent resorted to a false complaint.
CRM-M-6117-2026 (O&M)
9.

With regard to abovementioned complaint, the learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the complaint as well as evidence itself shows that the alleged incident had taken place in the year 2009, whereas the complaint was filed in the year 2018, i.e. after a gap of more than 09 years,
and that the abovementioned inordinate delay has not been explained by the respondent.

As per learned counsel for the petitioner in view of above, at the threshold itself the complaint should have been dismissed by the learned trial Court, but the learned trial Court took cognizance on the abovementioned complaint and summoned the petitioner.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner has referred to the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of 'Hasmukhlal D. Vora & Anr. V/s The State of Tamil Nadu' 2024(2) SCC (Cri) 632.
10.

sentences.text: In addition to above, the learned counsel for the petitioner has also contended that similar complaint was moved by the respondent before the Panchayat authority and with regard to above, a detailed enquiry was conducted, wherein it was found that allegations against the petitioner with regard to misappropriation of funds were not true and the petitioner was duly exonerated.

According to learned counsel for the petitioner, despite the fact that the Government authorities in Roshan Lal vs State Of Punjab And Another on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44536313/
2 enquiry found the petitioner to be innocent, and the complaint to be false, the learned trial Court on account of wrong appreciation of fact as well as law summoned the petitioner.

sentences.text:
As per learned counsel for the petitioner, the abovementioned process adopted by the respondent is nothing but an abuse of process of law, and therefore, there CRM-M-6117-2026 (O&M) is need for indulgence &
interference of extraordinary jurisdiction vested in this Court.
11. The record has been perused carefully.
12. A perusal of record shows that in the present case, cognizance against the petitioner has been taken by virtue of impugned order, on appreciation of documentary evidence.

The documentary evidence adduced by the respondent before the learned trial Court was very specific qua the fact that on few particular dates, Pyara Singh was shown to be a worker at two places and for both the jobs,
wages were paid to him.

Since it is not possible for one person to work at two different places at the same time, and draw double wages, this plea of the respondent seems to have got force that by forging the documents, double payment had been made by the petitioner, and thus, the public funds were misappropriated by playing fraud.

13. As far as arguments with regard to enquiry conducted by Panchayat Department is concerned, in view of fact that the evidence placed on record before the learned trial Court was not properly considered by the Department authorities, the abovementioned enquiry report cannot come in the way of summoning order passed by the learned trial Court, on appreciation of documentary evidence.
Otherwise also, there is no bar for learned trial Court to take cognizance with regard to an act, wherein departmental authorities have failed to take any action.
In the present case, the plea with regard to delay in filing of complaint has also been taken qua the abovementioned complaint.

It is relevant to note here that on the enquiry report of Departmental authorities, which was initiated at the instance of respondent, final decision was taken in the last month of December, 2014 and within four years of abovementioned enquiry report,
the complaint was filed.

Otherwise also, the offence for which the petitioner has been summoned is punishable for imprisonment up to 07 years, and therefore, there is no bar of limitation for taking cognizance for such an offence.

15. In view of abovementioned facts and circumstances of the present case it is apparent on record,
that on proper appreciation of facts and evidences, a right view has been taken by the learned trial Court, while taking cognizance against the petitioner.

As far as the applicability of law propounded by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of 'Hasmukhlal D. Vora' (supra), is concerned in view of the fact that the factual matrix of the present case is altogether different, it is hereby held that the abovementioned principles are not applicable to the present case.

16. With regard to scope and indulgence of this Court for exercising extraordinary jurisdiction, the guiding principles, wherein extraordinary jurisdiction for quashing of FIR can be exercised, have been laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Neeharika CRM-M-6117-2026 Roshan Lal vs State Of Punjab And Another on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44536313/
3 (O&M) Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra and others 2021 SCC Online SC 315.

sentences.text: It casts an onerous and more diligent duty on the court;

In addition to above, in the case of 'State of Haryana Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal', 1991(1) RCR 383, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India after reviewing large number of cases on the question of quashing of FIR has laid down that the FIR can be quashed in the following circumstances:-
a) Where the allegations made in the First Information Report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
b) Where the allegations in the First Information Report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the F.I.R. do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.
Roshan Lal vs State Of Punjab And Another on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44536313/
4 c) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.
d) Where the allegations made in the F.I.R. or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

entities.text: Roshan Lal vs State Of Punjab And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: e) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and CRM-M-6117-2026 (O&M) continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

f) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge.

18. Taking into consideration the factual matrix of the case, the issues involved in the present petition and the relevant laws, it is hereby held that in the present case when the case is at the initial stage, once the cognizance has been taken by the learned trial Court after due appreciation of preliminary evidence, and apparently there is no perversity or illegality in the order passed by the learned trial Court, it is hereby held that there is no scope for indulgence or interference in the impugned order.
Thus the present petition being devoid of merit deserves dismissal.
The same is hereby dismissed, accordingly.
19. Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, stand(s) disposed of, accordingly.
(SURYA PARTAP SI  JUDGE  04.02.2026

"a) The power of quashing should be exercised sparingly with circumspection, as it has been observed, in the 'rarest of rare cases (not to be confused with the formation in the context of death penalty).

d) Quashing of a complaint/FIR should be an exception rather than an ordinary rule;
e) Save in exceptional cases where non-interference would result in miscarriage of justice, the Court and the judicial process should not interfere at the stage of investigation of offences;
